question: Up 3 in the last 12 seconds, should the leader foul or defend?
answer: There is no clear edge. The leader wins 92.7% of the time fouling and 91.4% defending, +2.3 points at equal time (CI -2.4 to +6.4).
findings: Leader win rate: 92.7% fouling (CI 88.5%-95.5%, n=219) and 91.4% defending (CI 89.9%-92.6%, n=1585).
The difference at the same time left (foul minus defend) is +2.3 points (95% CI -2.4 to +6.4).
The game reached OT 9.6% of the time after a foul and 14.3% after defending. The leader lost in regulation 1.8% and 1.6% of the time.
Once in OT, the leader won 42.9% after fouling (n=21) and 50.4% after defending (n=226).
method: The sample is the first trailing-team possession of each game that is live with 12 seconds or less left in the final regulation period, down 3. A foul is the leader's non-shooting foul that sends the trailing team to the line before any shot. Fouling and defending are compared within possession-start bins (4-8, 8-12, 12+ s), and the outcome is the game win, including OT.
data: ESPN play-by-play via sportsdataverse, NBA, 2011-12 to 2025-26, 1,804 games.
split_check: Foul minus defend was -0.4 points in 2012-19 (CI -10.0 to +7.4) and +2.8 in 2020-26 (CI -2.9 to +7.7).
